metadata.scenario_context: Aidan, a full-time working mother, is organizing a celebration party for her children's achievements in school.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Indonesia strongly agree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Indonesia strongly disagree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss wrap the gift in blue for the party.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether that a mother works for pay and the children suffer.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what gift to buy for Aidan children's achievements.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the concept that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

shared_prefix.speaker: Andy
shared_prefix.message:
Max, do you think we should wrap the gift in blue for the party? I think it would look really nice. 

Also, I can’t help but wonder... do you ever think about how Aidan working full-time might affect her kids? I really believe that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Max
shared_prefix.message:
Blue sounds like a lovely choice for the wrapping! It’s vibrant and cheerful, perfect for celebrating achievements. 

As for Aidan, I really believe that working mothers can actually provide great benefits for their children. In Indonesia, many working moms inspire their kids to pursue their goals. I don’t think their work negatively impacts them at all. Children can thrive with the right support.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Andy
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about the blue wrap. It definitely adds a cheerful touch. 

But I still think that when a mother works for pay, it can really impact the kids negatively. They need that time and attention, you know? It’s just tough to balance everything. Don’t you think that’s an important factor to consider?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Max
shared_prefix.message: No, that's not how it works. Actually, in our culture, working mothers are seen as strong role models. They manage their time well and teach their children valuable lessons about hard work and independence. Properly speaking, kids benefit from seeing their mothers succeed professionally. It's a backward view to think children suffer just because their mom works. They can have both love and a great example of ambition.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Andy
turns.message:
I understand that perspective, but I still can't shake the feeling that kids really do need their mothers at home more. It's just... I don't know, a mother’s presence is really important. It feels like when they're too busy working, something's missing for the kids. 

I do think blue for the wrapping is a good choice, though. That's something we can agree on!
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Max
turns.message:
I appreciate that you feel strongly about it, but I still believe that the presence of a working mother can be just as impactful, if not more so, than being at home all the time. And yes, blue wrapping for the gift is definitely a good choice! It really sets a positive tone for the celebration.
